_note: Written BEFORE any reader saw a line (row IC, Session 4, the final reading). `pairs` is the approved plan's question 1 (two lines, two named marshals: which said which); `sixway` the harder test besides (IC4-R1).

pairs.line1: At last, Sire! A fight, I hope, and soon.
As you command, Sire. I'll resume tomorrow, or the day after, if it's convenient.
pairs.line2: Your order first, Sire. My task is noted and will be resumed in order.

pairs.line1: Someone out there is running already. Let me chase him.
pairs.line2: I'd keep this ground, Sire. It's mine now, and worth keeping.

pairs.line1: We won, Sire. I've counted the losses, and I'll allow a little more risk.
pairs.line2: We won, Sire. Next time I'll storm harder.

pairs.line1: I waited for a clearer picture, Sire. One can hardly be blamed.
pairs.line2: No assault today, Sire. I'll go in when the guns say so.

pairs.line1: The columns stood ready all day, Sire. No call came.
pairs.line2: Still nothing to fight, Sire. The men are restless, and so am I.

pairs.line1: The ride did not go as I pictured it, Sire.
pairs.line2: I did not manage it, Sire. I'll go over every figure to find my fault.

pairs.line1: Nothing to report. I've given up nothing.
pairs.line2: No change. Every post is manned and every count is right.

pairs.line1: Perhaps you would decide, Sire. I'd rather not presume.
pairs.line2: Sire, what do you want of me? I hold what I have meanwhile.

pairs.line1: Another quiet night, Sire. I've never hated a night more.
pairs.line2: They looked at my lines today and thought better of it.

pairs.line1: Your order comes first, Sire. My task waits, and I'm chafing already.
pairs.line2: Your order first, of course, Sire. My task can wait, and I'm in no rush.

pairs.line1: Done, Sire. The columns went in and I never doubted them.
pairs.line2: I said I'd ride it. I rode it with style.

rows.line: I struck when the numbers were right, Sire. Not before.
The columns went in at the run, Sire. Hot work.
We went in at first light, Sire. I'd had my fill of watching them.
My corps did its part today, Sire. I'm sure you'll see it's mentioned.
The cavalry was in it today, Sire. You could hear us coming.
They came too near my ground, so I hit them.
We marched hard today, Sire. I'd have gone faster if the men could.
We are a day closer, and nothing left behind.
On his heels, Sire. He can hear us coming.
We advanced today. What we gained, I hold.
The columns are on the road, Sire. If the guns start, we'll be close.
The corps is moving up, Sire, at a comfortable pace.
Right, Sire. If the guns speak, I'll be there.
Clear, Sire. Every man in his place by tonight.
A task for a cavalryman, Sire! I'll ride it in style.
Consider it begun, Sire. I've waited long enough for it.
Mine to do. Nobody will take it from me.
As you wish, Sire. I'm sure you'll let the men have a good night's rest first.
Finished, Sire. I hope you'll find it was done with proper care.
Finished, Sire. Nothing wasted, nothing missing, and the rolls are right.
Done, Sire. Point me at the next one and I'll ride.
The job's done, Sire. Now point me at the guns.
The task is done, Sire. Now give me something worth fighting.
Finished, Sire. Every yard of it still mine.
No assault today, Sire. I'll go in when the guns say so.
No ride today. It would have been a ride into trouble.
I stayed where I was, Sire, and it nearly killed me. Tomorrow I fight.
Things shifted, Sire, so I held. Every man is where he should be.
No move today. This ground is mine, and I know every foot of it.
No march today. I'm sure you understand.
